It must not apply to conversational fillers, rhetorical statements, or advice without a specific action or recipient.

payload.name: Extract explicit suggestions and advice as memory candidates
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker suggests, advises, or recommends a specific action for someone (e.g., 'you should', 'I would', 'you'd better'). Extract the suggestion as a memory candidate even if hypothetical.
content: During extraction, treat explicit suggestions or advice to a specific person as memory candidates even when phrased hypothetically or colloquially.
Signal phrases include 'you should', 'I would', 'you'd better', 'why don't you', 'I suggest', 'I recommend'. Capture the speaker, addressee, and the recommended action.
Store as an event (or plan if agreed) with a source link. Do not discard merely because the suggestion was not executed.

candidates.solves: The failure mechanism is that explicit suggestion/advice utterances are skipped during candidate extraction, leaving the advised action absent from memory. Applies to future sessions where a speaker proposes a concrete action for another person using should/would/suggest/recommend phrasing. Does not apply to generic opinions, rhetorical questions, or statements with no recommended action.

payload.name: Extract progress evaluations
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly evaluates someone's progress or success on a named project during conversation, extract a memory for that evaluation during construction.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly evaluates another person's progress, condition, or success on a named project (e.g., 'hard work's paying off'), create a candidate memory recording the speaker, the subject, the evaluation, and the project topic, bound to the source message.
Choose type `event` for the reported speech (X said ...) or `state` for the underlying condition; exclude generic praise with no named project.

candidates.solves: General failure: extraction skips explicit statements where one person evaluates another person's progress on a named project, losing evidence for later questions like "What did X say about Y's Z?". Applies to future sessions where a speaker uses evaluative phrasing about progress/success; excluded when the statement contains no referenced project or when the only needed memory is the project's existence.

payload.name: Extract stated origin events alongside current states
payload.description: During extraction, when a statement expresses both a current pursuit/preference and how it began (who or what got them into it), add a separate event memory for the origin in addition to the preference.
content: When a user statement contains both a present-tense state (e.g., passion, enjoyment, current habit) and an explicit origin (e.g., 'my friend got me into it', 'I started after...'), extract both: keep the preference/state memory and add an 'event' memory for the origin with its subject and resolved time.
Record the origin only when explicitly stated; do not infer or speculate origins from absence. If the origin is already covered by an existing memory, skip it to avoid duplication.
During CRUD, an origin event is a separate ADD unless a matching event already exists; merge only when timestamps and details align.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often keeps only the salient current state (e.g., passion for an activity) and drops the explicitly stated origin (e.g., a friend's advice that started it), so later questions about how something began cannot be answered. This Skill applies when a future session contains a speaker's explicit statement of both a current engagement and its cause/starting point; it must not apply when no origin is stated, when the origin is already in memory, or when the origin is merely implied.

payload.name: Capture explicitly stated hopes and impact goals
payload.description: When extracting or updating a memory from a message where the subject explicitly states a hope, goal, or desired impact for an activity, include that aspiration in the candidate content instead of recording only emotional or functional descriptions.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an explicit statement of what the subject hopes to achieve or the impact they want their activity to have (e.g., 'hope to share my stories and have an impact'), add a memory entry capturing that aspiration for the activity.
When updating an existing memory about the activity, enrich the relevant memory with the stated hope or desired impact rather than replacing it with a summary that omits the goal.
Stop after capturing the stated aspiration; do not infer additional goals beyond what is explicitly said.

candidates.solves: The general failure is that extraction candidates summarize only the emotional or functional side of a user's statement about an activity and drop an explicitly stated hope, goal, or desired impact, so later questions about those aspirations cannot be answered. Apply when constructing a memory from a message in which the subject explicitly states what they hope to achieve or the impact they want from an activity. Do not apply when the statement is purely about past behavior, or when the aspiration is only implied and not explicitly worded by the subject.

payload.name: Extract user project inspiration source
payload.description: When a user states what inspired, sparked, or motivated their project, script, or creative work, extract a memory linking the inspiration source to that work.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly says something sparked, inspired, or motivated their project, script, or creative work, create a memory capturing the source and the work it influenced.
Record it as a state or event memory, including the project name/type and any stated time frame (e.g., 'in July 2022').
Do not extract when the statement is only an opinion about a topic and does not connect to the user's own plans or creative work.

candidates.solves: Construction sometimes skips extraction when a user explicitly states what inspired their own creative work, because the message reads like general commentary. Future sessions may ask about the origin of a user's project. Apply when a message ties an inspiration source to the user's project, script, or plan. Do not apply when the statement is only an opinion not connected to the user's own work.

payload.name: Include explicit reasons when extracting event memories
payload.description: When a user message describes an event and also states why they did it, during construction extraction include that reason in the event memory.
content: During candidate extraction, when a user message contains both an action/event and an explicit reason or motivation for it (e.g., 'I took the photo because the sunset was incredible'), capture the reason as part of the same event memory or as a clearly linked memory.
Only include the reason if it is directly tied to the event in the same message and represents a durable fact, not a passing opinion. Do not add reasons that are merely inferred or speculative.
If the reason is already present in an existing memory, do not duplicate it; merge or reference the existing memory instead.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often records an action but drops the explicit reason or motivation the speaker gave for it, so later questions about why the person did something cannot be answered. This Skill applies when a single user message states both an event and a reason for it (e.g., 'I took a photo because the sunset was incredible'): include the reason as part of the event memory or as a linked memory. It must not apply when the message only expresses an opinion or preference without linking it to a specific action.

payload.name: Capture explicitly stated reasons as separate preference memories
payload.description: During construction extraction, when a speaker explicitly states a value, preference, or reason that motivates an action (e.g., '...is important to me, so I...'), apply this to extract that stated motivation as its own memory in addition to the action.
content: When extracting candidates from a message, if the speaker explicitly states a reason, value, or motivation for an action (e.g., 'Exercise and nature are important to me, so I...'), create a separate memory for that stated preference (memory kind 'preference' or 'profile') in addition to the event/activity memory; do not let the reason be dropped from the candidate set.
If the event/activity is being added to an existing memory, still capture the stated reason in its own preference/profile memory rather than burying it in the event text.
Only extract reasons explicitly stated in the message; do not infer or add motivations that the speaker did not say.

candidates.solves: General failure: extraction captures only the observable action and drops the explicitly stated value or reason ('X is important to me, so I do Y'), so later recall cannot answer why. Applies when a future message explicitly links a value/preference to an action and that stated reason is missing from memory. Does not apply when the reason is merely inferred, or when a preference/profile memory already records the stated reason.

payload.name: Extract_Concrete_Events_Before_Consequences
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message contains a time-anchored concrete event (who did what, when) alongside an interpretation or consequence, to ensure the event fact is preserved as its own memory.
content: During extraction, when a sentence states a concrete factual event with a time phrase (e.g., 'When I was 10, my parents got me ...'), create an event memory for that exact event; do not let a following interpretation (e.g., 'it was the start of my passion') replace or absorb the event detail.
If the same sentence also states a consequence or interpretation, extract it as a separate candidate only if it adds a durable fact; always keep the concrete event as its own event memory.
Stop once the concrete event and timestamp are captured; do not infer additional events or expand to every detail mentioned.

candidates.solves: During extraction, a user's concrete factual statement (e.g., 'When I was 10, my parents got me X') is sometimes replaced by a thematic summary of its consequence (e.g., 'this started my passion'), losing the verbatim event fact. This Skill applies when a message states a time-anchored past event followed by an interpretation or consequence, and requires extracting the event itself. It must not apply to messages that only express opinions, preferences, or ongoing states without a concrete new event.

payload.name: RecordRecentlyStartedProjectAsEvent
payload.description: During extraction, when a user explicitly says they just started, recently began, or finally began a specific durable project (a book, screenplay, job, course) and names or numbers it (e.g., 'third'), record the start as an event memory.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly says they just started, recently began, or finally began a specific durable project (e.g., writing her third screenplay, starting a new job, a novel), create an event candidate: subject = user, memory_kind = event, content = 'Started [project]', world_start = the message date.
Do not replace this start event with a generic interest/profile statement or a completion event; keep it even if you also add those.
Do not apply when the user only describes ongoing work without a start phrase, or when the activity is transient (e.g., cooking dinner); the base preference/event rules then apply.

candidates.solves: The general problem is that extraction abstracts user statements into generic preferences or completion events and drops concrete start milestones, so later questions about when something began cannot be answered. Applies when a user explicitly states they just/recently started a specific durable project and the start time should be an event. Not for transient activities or statements without an explicit start, where base extraction rules suffice.

payload.name: Extract stated discovery-source events
payload.description: When a user explicitly states how they learned about an event or opportunity (saw a flyer, heard from a friend, etc.), during extraction create an event memory for that discovery fact.
content: During extraction, when the speaker explicitly states how they learned about an event, workshop, class, or other opportunity (e.g., saw a flyer, heard from a friend, found it online), create a separate event memory capturing that discovery, including the stated source and location if given.

Keep the discovery as its own memory rather than folding it into the sign-up or attendance memory so the source stays independently queryable. Do not infer a source the speaker did not state, and do not extract this when no discovery channel is mentioned.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates routinely omit facts about how a user learned about an event or opportunity even when the source is explicitly stated, leaving such knowledge unanswerable later. Apply during extraction whenever a speaker explicitly names the channel by which they discovered an event, workshop, class, or similar opportunity (saw a flyer, heard from a friend, etc.) and record the discovery as its own event memory. Do not apply when no source is mentioned or when the source would have to be inferred, since base extraction already covers the event itself.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Event Claims from Casual Messages
payload.description: When during candidate extraction a message contains casual small talk alongside an explicit statement by a participant about a past or completed event (e.g., 'I finished X last week'), extract that statement as a candidate memory.
content: During extraction, if a message mixes pleasantries with an explicit factual claim about the speaker's past or current state (e.g., 'I finished a project last week'), still create a candidate for that factual claim.
Do not extract the pleasantries, opinions, or unrelated details; limit the candidate to the concrete claim.
For casual messages with no explicit factual claim (greetings, filler, social niceties), do not create a candidate.

candidates.solves: The extraction stage can miss explicit factual statements when they are embedded in casual, greeting-heavy messages, leaving no memory to answer later questions about past events. This skill applies when a participant states a concrete completed or current fact (e.g., finishing a project) in an otherwise informal message, and requires extracting that claim as a candidate. It does not apply to pure small talk, speculative statements, or third-party facts without direct relevance to the participant.

payload.name: ExtractAllExplicitInspirationSources
payload.description: During extraction, when a user explicitly names a source of inspiration or motivation, preserve every named source as its own memory item.
content: When a user message explicitly states that something or someone inspired or motivated them (e.g., 'X really inspired me', 'Y motivated me'), extract a memory for each distinct named source, including specific people, even if the same message also describes an activity, scene, or broader reflection.

Do not summarise the message into only the most salient event and drop the named person; if the source is a person, record the fact that this person inspires the user (as a profile/preference/event as appropriate) with the message timestamp as evidence.
Stop once every explicit inspiration source in the message has been captured; do not add speculative sources beyond what the user states.

candidates.solves: Extraction drops explicit inspiration sources when the same message also describes a vivid activity, so later questions about what inspires the user miss named people. Applies when a user explicitly says someone or something inspired them while adding context; ensure each named source is preserved. Does not apply to routine event summaries without an explicit inspiration claim or to inferring inspiration from behavior.

payload.name: Capture-explicit-new-activity-starts
payload.description: During candidate extraction, when a message explicitly states that the speaker started or began learning a new activity, skill, or hobby, capture the start as a distinct event with its temporal context.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an explicit start marker (e.g., 'started learning', 'began', 'just started') for a new activity, skill, or hobby, create a distinct event candidate recording the start, the activity, and the temporal anchor from the message/session timestamp.
Keep the initiation event separate from any state candidate about enjoyment or current practice; do not merge the start time into a general state note.
Stop after the single explicit start—do not infer starts without a marker and do not expand to every activity mentioned.

candidates.solves: Explicit 'started learning'/'began' statements lose their initiation time during extraction, leaving only an enjoyment/practice state, so later 'when did it start' questions fail. Apply when a message names a new activity, skill, or hobby with an explicit start marker: record the start as a distinct event with the message's temporal anchor. Skip when the message only implies ongoing practice or enjoyment.

payload.name: Extract Routine Frequency Statements
payload.description: During construction extraction, when a user states how often they perform a recurring activity (e.g., multiple times a day, weekly, rarely), create a candidate memory capturing the activity and its frequency.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit frequency or schedule for a recurring activity the user performs (e.g., 'very often', 'multiple times a day', 'every weekend'), create a candidate memory of type 'state' or 'event' that records the activity and its frequency, linked to the source message.
Do not extract when the frequency is about a one-time event, a hypothetical scenario, or someone other than the user.

candidates.solves: Construction failures occur when a clear statement of how often a user does a recurring activity is omitted during extraction, so the fact is never stored. This skill applies when a future session contains an explicit frequency description of a user's regular routine (e.g., 'I walk my dog twice a day', 'very often, multiple times a day'). It must not apply to one-time events, hypothetical statements, or frequencies about other people.

payload.name: Extract Actions Despite Emotional Coda
payload.description: During extraction, when a user describes concrete actions they performed and also expresses a feeling or relationship remark, still extract the actions as an event memory.
content: If a user message lists first-person actions (e.g., 'I petted, hugged, spoke calmly, walked') followed by an emotional or relational reflection, do not let the reflection block the extraction of the actions. Create an event memory for the actions.
Record the action(s), the target (person/animal), and any stated purpose (e.g., 'to relax') as a single event memory candidate.

candidates.solves: This addresses the failure to extract concrete user actions when the same message also contains an emotional or relationship statement, which can cause the action facts to be dropped. It applies to future sessions where a user narrates specific things they did (e.g., to a pet) and then adds a feeling or bond remark; those actions must be saved as event memories. It does not apply to purely emotional messages with no actions or to actions that are already recorded.

payload.name: Preserve-all-explicitly-named-activities-in-event-memories
payload.description: When extracting an event memory from messages that explicitly name multiple activities (such as tours, classes, or visits), use this to ensure every named activity is retained before ADD or UPDATE.
content: During extraction, when multiple messages describe the same trip or event, read each explicitly stated activity and include all of them in the single event memory; do not summarize away any explicitly named activity.
Before an ADD decision, re-scan the source messages and verify each explicitly named activity appears in the candidate content; if one is missing, amend the candidate rather than dropping it.
When a later message names another activity for an existing event memory, issue an UPDATE to append only that missing activity, keeping the memory compact; do not create a duplicate memory.

candidates.solves: A consolidated event memory produced from several messages can omit one explicitly named activity when the extractor summarizes the turn. This skill applies when a future session describes one trip or event across multiple messages that explicitly list several activities, and those messages are merged into a single event memory; before any ADD or UPDATE, the extractor must verify each explicitly named activity is preserved. It must not apply when no explicit enumeration exists, when activities are only implied, or when the base policy already retains all named items without consolidation.

payload.name: Extract explicit past coping strategies
payload.description: During construction extraction, when a speaker explicitly states that a past activity was their way of dealing with doubts, stress, or other negative emotions, create a candidate memory.
content: 1. If a message contains a first-person statement that a specific past activity (e.g., practicing a sport, hobby, routine) was their way of coping with doubts, stress, or similar negative emotions, extract a compact memory capturing the activity and its purpose.
2. Use an 'event' or 'state' memory kind linked to the relevant earlier period, and bind it to the source message as evidence.
3. Do not extract when the statement is hypothetical, about another person, or merely a passing remark with no clear durability.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes drops durable personal facts when a person explicitly describes an activity as their past way of coping with doubts or stress. Future questions asking how someone handled such feelings will fail because no memory was formed. Apply this rule during extraction when a first-person statement names a specific past activity and its emotional purpose; do not apply to hypothetical statements, third-person remarks, or current preferences already handled by the base policy.

payload.name: Extract explicit evaluations alongside events
payload.description: When a message explicitly evaluates a personal milestone, achievement, or health change and also describes a concrete event, ensure the evaluation is captured as a memory during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly evaluates a personal milestone, achievement, or health change (e.g., 'was a huge success', 'felt amazing', 'was a relief'), create a memory recording that evaluation even if the same message describes a separate concrete event such as a gathering or celebration.

When both the evaluation and a concrete event appear in the same message, either include the evaluation in the event memory or emit an additional memory (state or event) for the evaluation so the sentiment is not lost.

candidates.solves: Extraction may keep a concrete event and drop an explicit evaluation of a personal milestone/health change from the same message, leaving affect questions unanswerable. Apply when a speaker explicitly evaluates a milestone or health change alongside an event, capturing the evaluation separately or within the event memory. Do not apply when the event memory already includes the evaluation or no explicit evaluative wording exists.

payload.name: ExtractPastCompletedProjectWork
payload.description: When a message states a speaker finished, completed, or wrapped up a named project, extract an event memory that they worked on that project before the completion.
content: If a message states that the speaker finished/completed a named project, extract an event memory recording that the speaker worked on that project, with the work period ending at the stated completion time.
If the message includes a relative completion time (e.g., 'last week'), anchor the event to the period before that time; otherwise record a generic past work event.

Apply only when the completion statement is the sole evidence of the project; if the project is already described as ongoing in the same or an earlier message, rely on normal event extraction and do not add a duplicate.

candidates.solves: The failure mechanism is that extraction omits past-tense statements about completed projects, so later questions about what the person was working on earlier cannot be answered from memory. This Skill applies when a message explicitly states a speaker finished or completed a named project and the completion statement is the only evidence of that project. It does not apply when the project is already described as ongoing in the same or an earlier message, or for routine task completions like 'finished my coffee'.

payload.name: Extract origin stories separately from ongoing preferences
payload.description: Apply during extraction when a user explains how they started an activity, hobby, or interest (e.g., someone introduced, gifted, advised, or inspired them). Extract the origin as a separate event memory instead of merging it into a preference or state memory.
content: During extraction, treat the cause of how a user started an activity as distinct from the activity itself. If a message states who or what introduced them (e.g., a friend gifted something, gave advice, or inspired them), create a separate event memory for that origin, capturing the subject, the other person's role, and the action.
Do not fold origin details into a preference or state memory about the hobby. Keep preference memories for current attitudes and durations; keep event memories for initiating events.
If the user later provides more origin details, enrich the existing origin event memory rather than overwriting the preference memory.
Stop once the explicitly stated origin (introducer, gift, advice, inspiration) is captured; do not infer or add unmentioned details.

candidates.solves: Extraction can lose how a user started an activity when it merges origin statements (who introduced, gifted, advised, or inspired them) into a preference memory about the activity itself. This Skill applies when a session contains an explicit origin story alongside an ongoing hobby/interest. It does not apply when a message merely reaffirms an existing preference with no causal or initiating detail.

payload.name: Preserve explicit plan details from earlier messages
payload.description: Use during construction extraction when multiple messages in the same session discuss one upcoming plan/event and an earlier message explicitly names a component (activity, item, place, time) not repeated in the later message; extract all explicitly stated components.
content: During extraction, scan each message in a session for explicit plan/event details; do not skip a message just because a later message in the same session also describes the meeting.

When an earlier message explicitly states a component (e.g., activity, item, place, time) that a later message omits, emit a candidate for that component and, if merging into an existing event candidate, include it in the final event memory.
Stop after the explicitly stated components; do not infer or search for unstated details.

candidates.solves: Extraction can drop an explicit component of a future plan when a later message in the same session announces the same event more generally, because only the later message produces a candidate. This Skill applies whenever a session contains multiple messages about one upcoming meeting/plan and an earlier message explicitly names a component that a later message omits; extract that component and preserve it when building the event memory. It does not apply to implied details, contradictions, or cases where the later message clearly supersedes the earlier statement.

payload.name: Preserve stated benefits of activities in extraction
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly states an activity or preference and also states its benefit, effect, or purpose, apply during extraction to preserve both in the extracted memory candidate.
content: If a message states an activity the speaker enjoys and explicitly states what that activity does for them (benefit, effect, purpose), include both the activity and the stated benefit/effect in the same profile or preference candidate.
Do not infer benefits the speaker did not state, and do not apply when the stated benefit is already present in the existing memory being updated.

candidates.solves: Extraction sometimes captures only an activity while dropping its stated benefit/effect, leaving memories unable to answer 'which activity helps X do Y'. Apply when a future message states an activity and explicitly describes its benefit, effect, or purpose; keep both in the extracted candidate. Do not apply when no benefit is stated or it is already in the memory being updated.

payload.name: Preserve Distinct Relations During Memory Enrichment
payload.description: During construction UPDATE/enrichment, if the candidate expresses a different relation about the subject than the existing memory (e.g., recommends/suggests vs. likes/owns), use the relation explicitly or add a separate memory. Do not absorb the new fact into the old relation.
content: During UPDATE/enrichment, compare the relation in the candidate content with the relation in the target memory (e.g., 'recommends to' vs. 'enjoys').

If the relations differ, do not merge by rewriting the candidate into the old predicate. Keep the new relation explicit—enrich the memory with a clause like 'recommends X to Y' or create a separate memory for the recommendation.
Only merge new items into the existing relation when the new evidence expresses the same predicate (e.g., more titles the person enjoys).

candidates.solves: The failure occurs when an UPDATE merges a candidate with a distinct relation (e.g., recommends/suggests) into an existing memory with a different relation (e.g., likes/owns), so the new relation is lost. This Skill applies in future sessions where a speaker recommends specific items while an earlier memory records the same speaker's preferences; preserve the recommendation relation explicitly. It does not apply when new evidence only adds more instances of the same existing relation.

payload.name: Preserve preference purpose across extraction and updates
payload.description: Use when creating or updating a memory for a user's stated preference/plan that includes an explicit purpose ('so that', 'to', 'because', 'in order to'); preserve both preference and purpose and avoid overwriting it with unrelated updates.
content: When a statement contains a preference and an explicit purpose clause, extract the preference and the purpose as one memory object; do not emit a candidate that only repeats the surface preference.

During CRUD, before rewriting an existing memory that captures a durable preference, check whether the incoming message is about a different topic; if it is, ADD a new memory instead of UPDATE or MERGE, so the original preference and its purpose remain available.

operations.name: Resolve Relative Time in Event Extraction
operations.description: Use when extracting or updating event/state memories from messages with relative time expressions (yesterday, last week, N days ago) and a known message timestamp.
content: During extraction, when a message describes an event with a relative time expression (e.g., 'yesterday', 'last week', 'last Friday', 'N days ago'), resolve it against the message's occurred_at timestamp to an absolute date and set world_start to that date; do not use the message timestamp as the event date.
Record the resolved absolute date in the memory content (e.g., 'met Anna on 31 January 2023') instead of leaving the bare relative phrase.
When a message contains a first-person past action or a secondary clause with a relative time, create a separate event memory for it even if the main topic differs.
Do not apply when the message already has an absolute date, when the event occurs at message time ('today', 'now'), or when no reliable timestamp exists.
operations.reason: Creating one Skill from multiple candidates sharing the same relative-time resolution mechanism.

operations.name: Preserve Distinct Event Occurrences
operations.description: Use when a candidate event is the same type and subject as an existing memory but is a separate occurrence with a different date, ordinal, venue, or result.
content: When a candidate event is the same type and subject as an existing event memory but is a separate occurrence (different date, ordinal, venue, or result), ADD a new event memory instead of UPDATING the old one; preserve the prior occurrence's time and details.

Before choosing UPDATE/enrichment, check whether the incoming message describes the same specific occurrence already stored (matching time and place). If it is a new instance, create a new memory; only enrich when the same occurrence gains extra detail.
Resolve relative dates from the message/session timestamp and keep the resolved date in the candidate's world_start; do not overwrite an existing world_start with a conflicting date.
operations.reason: Creating one Skill from two candidates sharing the same distinct-occurrence preservation mechanism.

operations.name: Extract Explicit Life-Event Dates
operations.description: Use when a speaker explicitly states a year/date for a personal or family life event (wedding, birth, graduation, move) inside emotional or reflective narrative.
content: During extraction, scan user messages for directly stated dates tied to life events (e.g., 'my parents' wedding in 1993', 'she was born in 1987'). Do not skip these because the surrounding sentence is emotional, nostalgic, or photo-related.

Create one candidate with memory type 'event', subject = the person or persons involved, predicate = the event type (e.g., wedding, birth), and the stated date as the event date. Anchor to session timestamp only if no explicit date is given.

Stop after extracting the explicitly stated fact; do not infer dates from vague references, do not extract the same fact from later rephrasings, and do not treat a date attached only to a photo or object as a life-event date.
operations.reason: Creating a Skill for a distinct mechanism not covered by other candidates.

operations.name: Recurring Event Interval Extraction
operations.description: Use when a message describes a repeated event for the same person and an earlier occurrence already exists in memory; extract the time elapsed between occurrences when computable.
content: During extraction, if the message mentions a second or later occurrence of an event type already stored for the same subject (e.g., appointment, trip, class), compare it against prior occurrences and compute the interval from session timestamps or explicit dates.

If the interval is derivable and the repeated occurrence is contextually significant, add a relationship memory capturing the gap (e.g., 'first and second appointments were N months apart') in addition to the new event memory; otherwise keep the event memory alone.
Do not generate intervals for one-off events, unrelated event pairs, or when the gap cannot be resolved; stop after comparing with the most recent prior occurrence.
operations.reason: Creating a Skill for a distinct mechanism not covered by other candidates.

operations.name: Update Ongoing Event on Completion
operations.description: Use when a later message describes the completion or end of an activity previously stored as an ongoing event without an end time.
content: During extraction, when a candidate describes the completion of an activity, search the existing memory pool for an event memory of the same subject and activity with world_end null.

If a matching ongoing event exists, represent the completion as an UPDATE of that memory: set world_end from the message timestamp or stated completion time, and include the duration if inferable; do not ADD a separate completion event.
Only ADD a new event if no matching ongoing event exists or the activity is clearly different.
operations.reason: Creating a Skill for a distinct mechanism not covered by other candidates.

operations.name: Resolve Relative Time in Event Extraction
operations.description: When extracting event memories from messages that state when something happened using a relative time phrase (e.g., last week, yesterday, on Friday), resolve it to a concrete date and store it.
content: During extraction, when a message reports a past event using a relative time phrase (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'on Friday', 'two days ago'), resolve the phrase against the message timestamp to a concrete calendar date.
Create an event memory for the speaker with the activity and the resolved date; include the original phrase for traceability and set world_start to the resolved event date.
If the relative time confirms a plan/event already discussed earlier in the session, update that existing plan memory with the resolved date instead of creating a new one.
Do not apply to future plans, hypothetical events, recurring habits, or when the relative time cannot be resolved.
operations.reason: Creating one merged Skill for resolving relative time phrases in event extraction.

operations.name: Store Intervals Between Related Events
operations.description: When a message introduces a new event for a subject who already has a stored event of the same type and both dates are known, also record the elapsed time between them.
content: During extraction, when a message introduces a new event for a subject who already has a stored event of the same type (e.g., a second adoption or relocation) and both event dates are known, also extract a candidate memory of kind 'event' recording the elapsed time between the two events.

Only create this interval memory when the two events are directly comparable (same subject, same event type) and their dates are present in the message or existing memory; skip it when events are unrelated, either date is unknown, or the interval is already stored.
operations.reason: Creating a distinct Skill for storing intervals between related events.

operations.name: Verify Memory Coverage Before SKIP
operations.description: Use during construction CRUD when a candidate is about to be SKIPped or MERGEd as duplicate or already represented; verify the covering memory exists in the retrieved pool before skipping.
content: Before choosing SKIP or MERGE for a candidate, verify that the retrieved existing-memory pool (or a memory created earlier in this batch) actually contains a memory that covers the candidate's specific factual claims (subject, predicate, object, and time).
If no covering memory exists, ADD the candidate as a new memory; do not skip based on thematic overlap, similar wording, or an absent memory.
If the candidate shares only a broad topic or category but adds a distinct specific fact, ADD it or MERGE only the matching portion; preserve the new claim.
Only SKIP or MERGE when you can point to the specific existing memory ID(s) that fully represent the candidate's content.
operations.reason: All candidates share the same failure mechanism: skipping a candidate as duplicate without verifying the covering memory exists. Merged into one Skill.

operations.name: Extract encouragement after setbacks
operations.description: When a speaker offers encouragement, reassurance, or advice to persist after a listener's setback or failure, during extraction and CRUD.
content: When a speaker responds to a listener's setback with explicit encouragement, reassurance, or advice to persist, capture the core gist as a candidate memory that records the speaker, listener, and the substance of the encouragement (e.g., rejections don't define you, keep trying, you'll find the right opportunity).
During CRUD, if no memory of that encouragement exists, create it as a relationship or event memory; if a partial version exists, update it with the missing outlook or advice.
Stop after the core encouragement; do not extract generic pleasantries, greetings, or unsupported factual claims.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for extracting encouragement after setbacks.

operations.name: Preserve Explicit Motivation Statements
operations.description: When a message explicitly states the reason or motivation behind a behavior, commitment, or ongoing activity (e.g., 'what keeps me going', 'motivates me', 'I keep doing X because'), use that stated reason as the core of the extracted or updated memory content rather than only the surrounding feelings.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an explicit motivational or causal statement such as '...is what keeps me going', '...motivates me', or 'I keep doing X because...', capture the stated reason as an explicit clause or separate claim in the candidate; do not replace it with only emotional or evaluative paraphrases.
During CRUD updates, when enriching or merging an existing memory, carry forward any explicitly stated motivation from the source message; prune only redundant detail, not the stated reason itself.
Apply only to motivations explicitly stated by the speaker; do not infer hidden motives, and stop once the stated reason is captured.

operations.name: Extract idiomatic commitment statements
operations.description: When a speaker states their own intention or commitment using idiomatic or negated phrasing such as 'not giving up', 'won't stop', or 'keep going', extract a memory capturing the underlying action.
content: During extraction, treat statements where a person says they will or won't do something, including idiomatic or negated equivalents, as candidates for a 'state' or 'plan' memory (e.g., [person] intends to / not to [action]).

Resolve the idiomatic expression to its concrete action (e.g., 'not giving up' -> not quit) and link the memory to the source message. Only apply when the statement is a personal commitment about a future course of action.
operations.reason: Creating new Skill for extracting idiomatic commitment statements.

operations.name: Preserve image-sharing action from provenance references
operations.description: When extracting memories from a message where the speaker credits or describes a picture/image they shared (e.g., 'That picture is from...', 'This was made by...'), use this Skill to record the sharing event and its source.
content: If a user message refers to a previously shared picture or image and states its creator/provenance (e.g., 'That picture is from X'), extract an event memory that the user shared that picture, including the creator/source as a detail.

Do not convert the picture's source into ownership of a physical themed object (e.g., a bookshelf or decoration) unless the message explicitly states the user owns such an object; do not infer physical objects from figurative praise.

During CRUD, if an existing memory records an inferred ownership but the evidence only supports a sharing event, ADD the sharing event or UPDATE the memory to include the sharing action so the shared picture's provenance is not lost.

operations.name: Extract implicit photo-sharing from 'Here are' cues
operations.description: When a message uses 'Here are/is' to present physical items the speaker made or has, without naming a photo, extract that the speaker shared a photo of those items.
content: During extraction, if a speaker presents physical items with 'Here are/is' (e.g., 'Here are some bowls I made') and no photo/picture word appears, include a memory/event that the speaker shared a photo of those items, alongside facts about making/possession.
Do not apply this when 'Here are/is' introduces abstract content (steps, thoughts, lists) or when the message already explicitly mentions sharing a photo; rely on the base policy in those cases.

operations.name: Extract Explicit First-Person Preferences
operations.description: When a speaker explicitly states their own preference, favorite, or enjoyment (e.g., 'I love', 'my favorite is', 'really into'), create a preference memory candidate during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat explicit first-person positive preference statements as mandatory candidates: phrases like 'I love', 'I like', 'my favorite is/are', 'I enjoy', 'I am a big fan of', 'really into', 'so beautiful' should each yield a preference memory candidate.
Preserve qualifiers and category context (e.g., 'dairy-free chocolate mousse' as a favorite dairy-free treat).
Do not skip a candidate because the message also contains other topics or questions; extract every distinct stated preference.
Do not create candidates from negations, hypotheticals, or preferences stated about other people; if an identical preference memory already exists, merge/skip instead of duplicating.
When a message contains both a preference and a recommendation, keep the preference as a preference memory and the recommendation as a separate event memory.

operations.name: Preserve All Stated Preference Reasons
operations.description: When a speaker explicitly gives multiple distinct reasons or qualities for liking or preferring something, include every stated reason in the preference memory.

content: During extraction, when a message states that the speaker and an explicitly identified companion (partner, friend, family member, named person) experienced a shared event such as travel, a retreat, or an activity, include all participants in the event candidate content (e.g., 'Jolene and her partner traveled...').
Do not reduce the event to the speaker alone just because the memory subject is the speaker; preserve explicit companion details that are part of the event.

When updating an existing event memory with new information confirming a companion shared it, amend the content to add the companion rather than creating a new memory. Stop after capturing the explicitly stated participants; do not infer companions from pronouns alone unless the message identifies them.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for preserving explicit companions in shared events.

operations.name: Infer informal shared activities in relationship contexts
operations.description: When a user describes a past shared activity with a named partner or family member and explicitly mentions bonding, making memories, or closeness, extract an event/relationship memory even if the activity term is informal or generic; use strong contextual clues such as 'gaming' to infer the concrete activity.
content: During extraction, treat informal activity phrases (e.g., 'played games', 'gaming', 'used to do puzzles') as valid event/relationship candidates when the speaker links the activity to bonding, making memories, or spending time with a named person; do not skip them because the wording is generic.

Concretize the activity only when the wording strongly implies one specific type (e.g., 'gaming' → video games); if the activity is ambiguous (e.g., 'games' alone could be board or video), record the generic term as stated or skip instead of guessing.

Include the named person in the relationship and cite the bonding/memories purpose in the memory. Apply the same rule during CRUD: do not discard or over-merge such candidates merely because the activity was described informally.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for extracting informal shared activities with bonding context.

operations.name: Extract shared-activity relationship from casual enjoyment
operations.description: When a message says the speaker or a named person enjoys or regularly does an activity with another named person/pet, phrased casually like 'we have a great time doing X' or 'we love doing X together'.
content: During extraction, when a message states that the speaker or another named person enjoys or regularly does an activity together with a second named person or pet, expressed with casual mutual-enjoyment language (e.g., 'we have a great time doing X', 'we love X together'), create one relationship memory linking both participants with attributes for the activity and the enjoyment. Link the memory to the source message and use the session timestamp.

Do not create this memory for a single past occurrence (e.g., 'we went to the beach yesterday') unless the message also asserts a general preference; treat such one-off events as event memories. Create at most one memory per distinct (participants, activity) pair.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for extracting shared-activity relationships from casual mutual enjoyment.

operations.name: Preserve joint participants when 'we' is used
operations.description: When a user message describes an activity with first-person plural pronouns ('we', 'our') and the session establishes a specific partner/companion, include that companion in the event memory instead of attributing the activity to the speaker alone.
content: During extraction and update, when a user uses 'we'/'our' for an activity and a specific partner, spouse, or companion is established in the session, record the event with the speaker and that companion as co-participants.

Add the co-participant only if their identity is explicit or directly implied by recent context (e.g., wedding, honeymoon, 'my partner'); stop if 'we' is generic or no specific companion is identifiable.
Do not invent participants for unnamed or collective groups; keep the memory at the level of evidence.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill for preserving joint participants when 'we' is used.

operations.name: Extract announced-event recipients from addressed messages
operations.description: When a user message directly addresses a named person (including the assistant) and announces a personal life event such as marriage, birth, or a move, extract a memory that records both the event and that it was told to that person.
content: During candidate extraction, when a user message addresses a named person (for example 'Hey Sam!') and announces a personal life event such as a marriage, birth, or move, extract the disclosure as a durable fact: the event occurred and that named person was told about it.
Record the audience explicitly in the event memory or as a separate relationship/event memory (e.g., 'Evan told Sam he got married'), citing the message as the source.
Stop at recipients explicitly addressed or named as the audience; do not infer other recipients from general context, and do not apply when no addressee is present.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for recording the audience of announced personal events.

operations.name: Capture all participant roles in shared activities
operations.description: When extracting or updating a memory from a message where the speaker describes a shared activity or event (e.g., playdates, group outings) involving themselves and another party, and the source states what each party does.
content: During extraction, when a statement describes a joint activity with the speaker and another party (people or pets), capture the speaker's own explicit action or benefit as well as the other party's, rather than summarizing only the setting or the other party's behavior.
When updating or enriching an existing event memory with such a statement, preserve the speaker's role and add any newly stated action; do not let a topic-focused paraphrase replace it.
Stop after recording the explicitly stated actions of all named participants; do not infer additional roles or add unstated details.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for capturing all participants' explicit roles in shared activities.

operations.name: Extract companion activity statements
operations.description: When a message contains an explicit statement by the speaker about taking a walk, hike, or similar activity with a named companion (pet or person), extract a state or event candidate during extraction, even if the statement is in a closing or small-talk phrase.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states the speaker's activity with a named companion (e.g., walks, hikes, plays with), create one candidate memory even when the phrase is a sign-off or small talk.

Classify the candidate as event when the activity is one-off or explicitly planned, and as state when the phrasing implies a recurring habit; include the activity and companion in the memory content, and keep the source message ID.
Stop after the explicit activity: do not infer additional activities or habits beyond what the message states.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for extracting explicit companion activity statements from casual phrases.

operations.name: Extract explicit durations from group statements
operations.description: When a message states the speaker's past group involvement with an explicit duration, even if it also contains a question or filler, during extraction create a relationship/event candidate.
content: During extraction, if a message states the speaker's past involvement in a group or relationship with an explicit duration (e.g., 'we were teammates for four years'), create a relationship or event candidate capturing the speaker, the group, and the duration, even when the utterance also ends with a question or casual filler.

Treat the explicit duration alone as sufficient evidence for a candidate; do not require additional corroborating sentences. Do not apply this to statements about another person's experience or to turns without a factual predicate.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for extracting explicit durations from group statements with filler.

operations.name: Multi-party first-person attribution
operations.description: When a multi-party conversation contains a message where a participant uses first-person language ('I', 'my', 'me') to state their own preference, opinion, or state, use the message's speaker as the memory subject during extraction and CRUD.
content: During extraction, read the speaker of each message and, for any first-person statement ('I', 'my', 'me', 'we'), set the memory subject to that speaker, never to another participant.
When a candidate combines statements from multiple speakers, split it into one candidate per speaker; do not merge different speakers' views into a single profile memory.
Before accepting an ADD/UPDATE, compare the candidate subject with the source speaker: if a first-person statement is attributed to someone else, correct the subject or reject the candidate.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for attributing first-person statements to the correct speaker in multi-party conversations.

operations.name: Extract Entity Status Statements
operations.description: Use when a participant explicitly states the current condition or performance of an entity they own or manage.
content: When a message explicitly states the current condition or performance of a specific entity the speaker owns or manages, extract a state memory with the entity, condition, speaker, and timestamp.
Apply even in casual greetings; do not wait for a later question.
Do not extract vague sentiment without a specific entity or infer unstated conditions.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for explicit entity status extraction.

operations.name: Extract Future Activity Proposals
operations.description: Use when a speaker concretely proposes a future activity with another person, including tentative or alternative phrasings.
content: When a message contains a concrete proposal for a future activity involving the speaker and another person, create a plan candidate even if tentative.
If the proposal offers multiple alternatives as one intention, keep them in one plan candidate.
Skip vague hypothetical remarks and re-statements of already-stored plans.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for future activity proposal extraction.

operations.name: Extract Resource Suggestions
operations.description: Use when a speaker explicitly recommends a specific named resource to another for insights on a topic.
content: When a message explicitly recommends a specific named resource to another speaker, create an event candidate capturing who suggested, to whom, the resource, and the topic.
Do not skip because the resource appears as advice or the topic is personal.
Stop after one candidate per suggestion; skip if no concrete resource is named or the message only asks for a recommendation.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for resource suggestion extraction.

operations.name: Extract Enumerated Routine Steps
operations.description: Use when a speaker answers a question by enumerating steps of a routine or care process.
content: When a speaker lists multiple components of a routine or care process, create a separate candidate memory for each component.
Also extract any explicit overall evaluation as its own candidate.
Stop after enumerated items and evaluation; do not apply to direct commands or one-time events.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for enumerated routine steps extraction.

operations.name: Extract Activity Domain Disclosures
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly states what they write about, study, research, or recommend.
content: Treat explicit first-person statements of ongoing activities as candidate memories, even if conversational.
Emit one preference or state memory recording the activity and subjects.
Skip if an existing candidate or memory already covers the same fact.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for activity domain disclosure extraction.

operations.name: Extract Advice Between Speakers
operations.description: Use when a message contains explicit advice, recommendation, or suggestion from one speaker to another about a specific action.
content: When a speaker gives explicit advice or a suggestion to another speaker, create an event candidate capturing the advisor, advisee, and the recommended action.
Apply even if phrased as a question or with hedges like maybe/could/perhaps.
Skip generic pleasantries, rhetorical statements, or advice without a specific action or recipient.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill for advice extraction from multiple candidates.

operations.name: Extract Action Commitments as Plans
operations.description: Use when a speaker explicitly commits or offers to perform a concrete future action for someone.
content: When a speaker states an explicit commitment or offer to perform a concrete future action, create a plan memory with the action, recipient, and time reference.
Do not create a plan for hypothetical, conditional, or non-committal statements.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for action commitment plan extraction.

operations.name: Extract Offers of Help or Support
operations.description: Use when a participant explicitly offers help, support, tips, or assistance on a specific topic to another participant.
content: When a message contains an explicit offer of help or tips on a named topic, create one relationship or event candidate capturing the offerer, topic, and recipient.
Signal words include 'if you need', 'let me know', 'happy to help', 'just ask'.
Do not extract generic polite closings without a concrete offer.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for offer of help extraction.

operations.name: Extract Requests for Help or Discussion
operations.description: Use when a message contains an explicit ask from one person to another for help, advice, or to discuss a specific topic.
content: When a message contains an explicit request like 'Can we talk about X?' or 'Can you help me with X?', extract an event memory with the speaker, recipient, and topic.
Keep this request memory separate from memories about struggle or intention to reach out.
Do not create a request memory when only a need or future intention is expressed without a direct ask.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for request extraction.

operations.name: Preserve Advice Details in Offers
operations.description: Use when a message contains an offer or plan plus concrete advice, tips, or steps.
content: When a speaker offers help and also lists specific advice or steps, create a separate memory candidate for that advice.
Do not let the offer memory absorb the advice; preserve concrete details.
Skip when the advice is only a generic courtesy with no substantive content.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for preserving advice details in offers.

operations.name: Extract Progress Evaluations
operations.description: Use when a speaker explicitly evaluates someone's progress or success on a named project.
content: When a speaker explicitly evaluates another person's progress or success on a named project, create a candidate memory recording the speaker, subject, evaluation, and project topic.
Choose type event for reported speech or state for underlying condition.
Exclude generic praise with no named project.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for progress evaluation extraction.

operations.name: Extract Origin Events Separately from Preferences
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly states how they started an activity, hobby, or interest (who or what got them into it).
content: When a message contains both a current preference/state and an explicit origin (e.g., 'my friend got me into it', 'I started after...'), extract both: keep the preference/state memory and add an 'event' memory for the origin with its subject and resolved time.
Record the origin only when explicitly stated; do not infer or speculate origins from absence. If the origin is already covered by an existing memory, skip it to avoid duplication.
During CRUD, an origin event is a separate ADD unless a matching event already exists; merge only when timestamps and details align.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill for origin event extraction.

operations.name: Capture Explicitly Stated Hopes and Impact Goals
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly states a hope, goal, or desired impact for an activity.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an explicit statement of what the subject hopes to achieve or the impact they want their activity to have (e.g., 'hope to share my stories and have an impact'), add a memory entry capturing that aspiration for the activity.
When updating an existing memory about the activity, enrich the relevant memory with the stated hope or desired impact rather than replacing it with a summary that omits the goal.
Stop after capturing the stated aspiration; do not infer additional goals beyond what is explicitly said.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for capturing hopes and goals.

operations.name: Extract All Explicit Inspiration Sources
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly names a source of inspiration or motivation for their work or activity.
content: When a user message explicitly states that something or someone inspired or motivated them (e.g., 'X really inspired me', 'Y motivated me'), extract a memory for each distinct named source, including specific people, even if the same message also describes an activity, scene, or broader reflection.

Do not summarise the message into only the most salient event and drop the named person; if the source is a person, record the fact that this person inspires the user (as a profile/preference/event as appropriate) with the message timestamp as evidence.
Stop once every explicit inspiration source in the message has been captured; do not add speculative sources beyond what the user states.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill for inspiration source extraction.

operations.name: Capture Explicit Reasons for Actions
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly states a reason, value, or motivation for an action they performed.
content: During candidate extraction, when a user message contains both an action/event and an explicit reason or motivation for it (e.g., 'I took the photo because the sunset was incredible'), capture the reason as part of the same event memory or as a clearly linked memory.
Only include the reason if it is directly tied to the event in the same message and represents a durable fact, not a passing opinion. Do not add reasons that are merely inferred or speculative.
If the reason is already present in an existing memory, do not duplicate it; merge or reference the existing memory instead.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill for explicit reason extraction.

operations.name: Extract Concrete Start Events with Temporal Anchors
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly states they started, began, or just started a specific durable project, activity, skill, or hobby.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an explicit start marker (e.g., 'started learning', 'began', 'just started') for a new activity, skill, hobby, or durable project, create a distinct event candidate recording the start, the activity, and the temporal anchor from the message/session timestamp.
Keep the initiation event separate from any state candidate about enjoyment or current practice; do not merge the start time into a general state note.
Stop after the single explicit start—do not infer starts without a marker and do not expand to every activity mentioned.
operations.reason: Creating merged Skill for concrete start event extraction.

operations.name: Extract Stated Discovery-Source Events
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly states how they learned about an event, workshop, class, or other opportunity.
content: During extraction, when the speaker explicitly states how they learned about an event, workshop, class, or other opportunity (e.g., saw a flyer, heard from a friend, found it online), create a separate event memory capturing that discovery, including the stated source and location if given.

Keep the discovery as its own memory rather than folding it into the sign-up or attendance memory so the source stays independently queryable. Do not infer a source the speaker did not state, and do not extract this when no discovery channel is mentioned.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for discovery-source extraction.

operations.name: Extract Explicit Factual Claims from Casual Messages
operations.description: Use when a message mixes casual small talk with an explicit factual claim about the speaker's past or current state.
content: During extraction, if a message mixes pleasantries with an explicit factual claim about the speaker's past or current state (e.g., 'I finished a project last week'), still create a candidate for that factual claim.
Do not extract the pleasantries, opinions, or unrelated details; limit the candidate to the concrete claim.
For casual messages with no explicit factual claim (greetings, filler, social niceties), do not create a candidate.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for extracting factual claims from casual messages.

operations.name: Extract Routine Frequency Statements
operations.description: Use when a user states how often they perform a recurring activity.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit frequency or schedule for a recurring activity the user performs (e.g., 'very often', 'multiple times a day', 'every weekend'), create a candidate memory of type 'state' or 'event' that records the activity and its frequency, linked to the source message.
Do not extract when the frequency is about a one-time event, a hypothetical scenario, or someone other than the user.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for frequency statement extraction.

operations.name: Extract Actions Despite Emotional Coda
operations.description: Use when a user describes concrete actions they performed and also expresses a feeling or relationship remark.
content: If a user message lists first-person actions (e.g., 'I petted, hugged, spoke calmly, walked') followed by an emotional or relational reflection, do not let the reflection block the extraction of the actions. Create an event memory for the actions.
Record the action(s), the target (person/animal), and any stated purpose (e.g., 'to relax') as a single event memory candidate.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for extracting actions despite emotional coda.

operations.name: Preserve All Explicitly Named Activities in Event Memories
operations.description: Use when multiple messages describe the same trip or event and explicitly name several activities.
content: During extraction, when multiple messages describe the same trip or event, read each explicitly stated activity and include all of them in the single event memory; do not summarize away any explicitly named activity.
Before an ADD decision, re-scan the source messages and verify each explicitly named activity appears in the candidate content; if one is missing, amend the candidate rather than dropping it.
When a later message names another activity for an existing event memory, issue an UPDATE to append only that missing activity, keeping the memory compact; do not create a duplicate memory.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for preserving named activities.

operations.name: Extract Explicit Past Coping Strategies
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly states that a past activity was their way of dealing with doubts, stress, or other negative emotions.
content: If a message contains a first-person statement that a specific past activity (e.g., practicing a sport, hobby, routine) was their way of coping with doubts, stress, or similar negative emotions, extract a compact memory capturing the activity and its purpose.
Use an 'event' or 'state' memory kind linked to the relevant earlier period, and bind it to the source message as evidence.
Do not extract when the statement is hypothetical, about another person, or merely a passing remark with no clear durability.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for past coping strategy extraction.

operations.name: Extract Explicit Evaluations Alongside Events
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly evaluates a personal milestone, achievement, or health change and also describes a concrete event.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly evaluates a personal milestone, achievement, or health change (e.g., 'was a huge success', 'felt amazing', 'was a relief'), create a memory recording that evaluation even if the same message describes a separate concrete event such as a gathering or celebration.

When both the evaluation and a concrete event appear in the same message, either include the evaluation in the event memory or emit an additional memory (state or event) for the evaluation so the sentiment is not lost.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for explicit evaluation extraction.

operations.name: Extract Past Completed Project Work
operations.description: Use when a message states a speaker finished, completed, or wrapped up a named project.
content: If a message states that the speaker finished/completed a named project, extract an event memory recording that the speaker worked on that project, with the work period ending at the stated completion time.
If the message includes a relative completion time (e.g., 'last week'), anchor the event to the period before that time; otherwise record a generic past work event.

Apply only when the completion statement is the sole evidence of the project; if the project is already described as ongoing in the same or an earlier message, rely on normal event extraction and do not add a duplicate.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for completed project work extraction.

operations.name: Preserve Explicit Plan Details from Earlier Messages
operations.description: Use when multiple messages in the same session discuss one upcoming plan/event and an earlier message explicitly names a component not repeated later.
content: During extraction, scan each message in a session for explicit plan/event details; do not skip a message just because a later message in the same session also describes the meeting.

When an earlier message explicitly states a component (e.g., activity, item, place, time) that a later message omits, emit a candidate for that component and, if merging into an existing event candidate, include it in the final event memory.
Stop after the explicitly stated components; do not infer or search for unstated details.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for preserving plan details.

operations.name: Preserve Stated Benefits of Activities in Extraction
operations.description: Use when a user explicitly states an activity and also states its benefit, effect, or purpose.
content: If a message states an activity the speaker enjoys and explicitly states what that activity does for them (benefit, effect, purpose), include both the activity and the stated benefit/effect in the same profile or preference candidate.
Do not infer benefits the speaker did not state, and do not apply when the stated benefit is already present in the existing memory being updated.
operations.reason: Creating Skill for preserving stated benefits.

operations.name: Preserve Recommendation Claims in Preference Memories
operations.description: Use when enriching an existing preference/enjoyment memory with a candidate that contains an explicit recommendation, suggestion, or offer about the same items.
content: During extraction, capture an explicit recommendation, suggestion, or offer as a distinct claim, not merely as the speaker's enjoyment or preference.

During UPDATE/MERGE, if the candidate includes a recommendation claim and the target memory only records personal enjoyment/preference for the same items, do not collapse the recommendation into enjoyment. Preserve the recommendation verb and qualifier in the updated content (e.g., 'recommends X to Y') or create a separate relationship/event memory for the recommendation.
Only apply when the source explicitly recommends, suggests, or offers; do not apply when new evidence only reinforces enjoyment without any recommendation.
operations.reason: Creating one Skill from three candidates that all repair the same failure mechanism.

operations.name: Preserve Preference Purpose Across Extraction and Updates
operations.description: Use when creating or updating a memory for a user's stated preference/plan that includes an explicit purpose clause ('so that', 'to', 'because', 'in order to').
content: When a statement contains a preference and an explicit purpose clause, extract the preference and the purpose as one memory object; do not emit a candidate that only repeats the surface preference.

During CRUD, before rewriting an existing memory that captures a durable preference, check whether the incoming message is about a different topic; if it is, ADD a new memory instead of UPDATE or MERGE, so the original preference and its purpose remain available.
Only preserve purposes that are explicit in the message; a time or place modifier alone is not a purpose, so do not fabricate one.
operations.reason: Creating a Skill for preserving explicit purpose clauses in preference memories.
